verdict_reason: _persistence_entropy is Atienza et al. Def. 3.1 exactly: PE = -sum p_i log2 p_i with p_i = l_i / sum(l). Against scipy.stats.entropy(base=2) -- which IS giotto-tda's kernel -- on five barcode families the worst disagreement is 2.2e-16, and the closed forms hold exactly (four equal bars -> 2.000000000000 = log2(4); two equal bars -> 1.0). The recent scale-invariance fix is real and correct: rescaling a barcode by 1e-16, 1, 1e16 and 1e300 now returns 1.846439344671 for all four, where the old absolute 1e-12 cutoff collapsed a 1e-14-scaled barcode to 0.
comparable_reason: The statistic is saturated against its own ceiling, so it has almost no cross-model dynamic range. Over 51 zoo checkpoints layer_0_pe_h0 spans 5.5018 to 5.5987 against the fixed analytic ceiling log2(49) = 5.6147 -- every model within 2.0% of the ceiling, total spread 1.73% of the mean -- and pe_h0_norm therefore spans only 0.9799 to 0.9971. Raising num_samples makes this WORSE, not better: on gpt2 pe_h0_norm goes 0.9979/0.9970/0.9775 at N=20 to 0.9991/0.9992/0.9974 at N=1000, and pe_simplification_ratio goes 0.9796 to 0.9983.
github_repo: giotto-ai/giotto-tda (reference kernel; not installed here) — Rucco/Chintakunta/Atienza released no code
github_reason: giotto-tda is not installed on this host, so I could not re-run the campaign-3 gtda parity here. I verified instead against scipy.stats.entropy(base=2), which is the kernel gtda's PersistenceEntropy calls, on five barcode families (uniform, linear, two-scale, degenerate, 50 random bars): max deviation 2.2e-16. The engine that produces the diagrams (ripser) was separately cross-checked against GUDHI 3.12.0 to 1.1e-07 under the topology_homology review.
paper_reason: Atienza et al. (Pattern Recognition 107:107509) state the definition and its bound rather than publishing a table this task's outputs map onto. What is reproducible and reproduced is the analytic ceiling implied by Def. 3.1: a barcode of m equal bars has PE = log2(m) exactly, and BLME returns 2.000000000000 for m = 4 and 1.000000000000 for m = 2, with zero error. The real-model values sit within 0.09% of that ceiling (gpt2, N=1000: 9.955543 vs log2(999) = 9.964341).
confounds_reason: Measured over 51 zoo checkpoints: layer_0_pe_h0 has rho = -0.101 with d_model, +0.018 with n_layers, -0.279 with vocab_size, -0.150 with log params. It is not an architecture proxy -- but that is because it is very nearly a constant (1.73% spread), not because it is measuring something scale-free and interesting. pe_simplification_ratio is worse: 0.9956 to 1.0136 across the zoo, i.e. noise around 1.
defects: CONFIG, and the recent change moved the wrong way: raising num_samples from 20 to 1000 INCREASED the saturation it was meant to fix, at 50x the forward passes. Measured on gpt2 -- pe_h0_norm per target layer 0.997889 / 0.997022 / 0.977510 at N=20, 0.999347 / 0.999016 / 0.996079 at N=100, 0.999117 / 0.999164 / 0.997416 at N=1000; the layer spread shrinks from 2.1% to 0.17% and pe_simplification_ratio moves from 0.9796 to 0.9983. The commit comment ('at 20 points an iid Gaussian already SATURATES the entropy ceiling') diagnoses the problem correctly and then applies the change that deepens it.

The saturation is structural, not a sample-size accident: H0 bars of a high-dimensional cloud are all of similar length (distance concentration), so p_i is near-uniform and PE is pinned at log2(m). Any fix has to change the statistic (report the deviation from a matched iid-Gaussian null at the same N and D, or use H1), not the point count.

CODE (latent, numeric): the total is summed before rescaling, so a barcode near the float64 ceiling overflows -- [1e308, 1e308] returns 0.0 where two equal positive bars must give exactly 1 bit. Unreachable on real barcodes (lifetimes are O(1) to O(100)) but a one-line fix (divide by max lifetime before summing).

CODE (minor): p = p[p > 1e-15] drops without renormalising, so [1, 1e-16] returns 0.0 against a true 5.3e-15 bits. The residual is below float64 resolution of the statistic (~5e-16 relative) and harmless; renormalising would cost nothing.

CODE (unsourced convention): pe_h0_full replaces the essential H0 bar with 2x the maximum finite lifespan. That factor is invented -- Atienza et al. do not define it and giotto-tda substitutes the maximum filtration value -- and it is exported as a first-class feature alongside pe_h0.

CODE (minor): pe_h0_norm divides by log2(len(lifespans_h0)) counted BEFORE the positive-lifetime filter inside the helper, so a diagram containing zero-length bars would normalise by a larger m than the entropy actually used. Does not fire at N >= 3 on real clouds (num_features_h0 = N-1 exactly).
CODE (minor, unreachable): pe_simplification_ratio is set to exactly 1.0 when the first-layer entropy is 0, inventing 'no change' where the ratio is undefined. Cannot fire for N >= 3.

The late target layer is hidden_states[num_layers], the POST-final-norm state, while the early one is a block output, so pe_simplification_ratio compares two different kinds of object. PE is scale-invariant so the norm's rescaling does not matter, but its mean subtraction and per-dimension affine do.
fix: 1) The _persistence_entropy change is correct -- keep it; it is a no-op on real barcodes (all p >> 1e-15), so no re-collection is needed for it. 2) Revisit the num_samples 20 -> 1000 raise: it costs 50x the forward passes and measurably reduces the metric's dynamic range (layer spread 2.1% -> 0.17% on gpt2). If the point is to escape saturation, report PE minus the PE of a matched iid-Gaussian cloud at the same (N, D), or drop pe_h0 in favour of pe_h1, which is the only key here with real spread (1.45 to 3.66 across the zoo). 3) Normalise by the maximum lifetime before summing to close the overflow path, and renormalise after the p > 1e-15 filter. 4) Source or drop pe_h0_full's 2x convention. 5) Read the late layer from a block output so pe_simplification_ratio compares like with like.
